title: Unrestricted GF(16) multiplication complexity
objective: Determine unrestricted XOR-AND multiplicative complexity of reduced GF(16) multiplication on 8 input bits and 4 outputs.

scope.primary_claim: Either construct and independently verify a reduced GF(16) multiplier with at most eight AND gates, or establish a complete nine-AND lower bound in the unrestricted Boolean model with explicit proof dependencies and reproducible finite certificates where used.
included: free XOR, NOT, constants, affine outputs, and arbitrary reuse of earlier nonlinear wires
exact circuit witnesses and all-256-input independent field-product comparisons
reviewed mathematical reductions with explicit coverage and proof dependencies
complete independent-method replay and every-case comparison of finite branch exclusions
primary-source prior-art comparisons before major campaigns and novelty claims
excluded: treating quadratic or bilinear lower bounds as unrestricted Boolean lower bounds
treating a scalar or output-pair witness as a full four-output field multiplier
transferring a lower bound for seven-output unreduced polynomial multiplication to the reduced field map without a proof
claiming world-first status from a bounded web search or a branch exclusion
claiming improved AES, silicon area, timing, power, energy, or leakage resistance from an AND count
scope.completion_boundary: The unrestricted question remains open locally until a full witness or a complete coverage proof passes the corresponding acceptance gate. Individual branch closures are retained as conditional results, not experiment completion. The completed AES simulation baseline remains a separate experiment.

allowed_strategies: algebraic proofs and wire-preserving normal forms
exhaustive enumeration with independently implemented mathematical checkers
SAT or SMT with independently checked certificates for negative claims
formalization or external review when useful
direct circuit construction, synthesis, and oracle replay
pivot to a better-supported research question with an explicit retained decision record
invariants: Boolean multiplication uses x_i^2=x_i; formal-polynomial and bilinear models are distinct
input-coordinate changes transport every old wire and the entire target jointly
scalar-equivalent replacement does not imply arbitrary-suffix wire-space preservation
all admitted scalar marks and old-space offsets remain covered unless a proved symmetry removes them
execution completion, independent replay, final audit, and publication are different states
unknown telemetry and physical metrics remain null

reference.encoding: a=sum(a_i*t^i), b=sum(b_i*t^i), outputs c_0..c_3 in the same polynomial basis; reduction polynomial 0x13
reference.oracle: independent carryless polynomial product followed by explicit reduction modulo 0x13, compared on all 16*16 operand pairs
reference.equivalence: A change of basis or common invertible affine input substitution must carry the full target and output decoder with it; mixing inputs does not impose a bilinear restriction.

correctness.unknown_policy: A missing audit, unavailable artifact, unresolved reduction, or unknown solver result remains explicitly pending or unknown; it is not a negative circuit result.

metrics.meaning: Count in the exact unrestricted Boolean DAG; XOR and affine operations are free in this model only.
Expected, produced, independently replayed, and final-audited counts are separate.
Reviewed reductions, finite independent replay, certificate checking, formalization, and external review are distinguished.
Agent, build, software enumeration, RTL simulation, and physical time remain separate; unavailable fields are null.
Bounded prior-art comparison is not proof that no prior result exists.
No PPA or security claim without a separate named target, implementation, and appropriate measurements.

research.title: Boyar-Find, Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions
research.fact: Sections 2.1 and 5 distinguish restricted quadratic circuits from unrestricted XOR-AND circuits; optimal quadratic existence for one/two outputs does not imply preservation of every actual circuit's wires.

research.title: MF-167 author research entry
research.fact: The author lists quadratic GF(16) complexity nine and unrestricted GF(16) complexity in [8,9]; publication priority and the complete evidence pack have not been independently audited here.

research.title: Morse, arXiv:2608.30238v1
research.fact: The author states unrestricted complexity nine for the seven-output unreduced four-term polynomial product, a different map from reduced four-output GF(16) multiplication; its Lean development has not been executed here.
